message: The emulation shows no failed checks. It's blocked because none of our eight AWS components have a native generator contract yet: the webhook endpoint, queue, DLQ, review worker, secret, drafts table, and the existing repo and Bedrock references all need implementation or an import plan. To answer the checker's question: no supported contract fits without changing the scope. The async word-count pipeline starts from S3 uploads, and bedrock-summary only handles direct text summaries, so forcing either one onto this design would quietly drop the webhook, read-only diff retrieval and line-linked drafts. That makes this product engineering work, and this artifact digest is the reproducer: a typed "pr-review" contract covering the webhook signature check, an SQS worker with a scoped Secrets Manager read, Bedrock Converse calls and conditional DynamoDB writes. I haven't changed the diagram because no edit to it can fill that gap. So let's settle the decision that defines that contract's permissions: should the system only ever store drafts for a person to read, or will a reviewer later approve drafts so they get posted to the PR?
